title: Industrial emission statistics
text:
ndustry (NACE B, C, D, E) is an important sector of the economy of the European Union (EU), helping to generate value added and jobs. At the same time, industrial sector activities also result in pressures on the environment such as emissions to air. This article compares the socio-economic and environmental performance of the EU's industry sector. Data extracted in January 2026 Planned article update: January 2027 Between 2010 and 2023, EU industrial emissions to air decreased significantly while industry's gross value added increased by 17%. Industry ([[Glossary:Statistical_classification_of_economic_activities_in_the_European_Community_(NACE)|NACE]] B, C, D, E) is an important sector of the economy of the [[Glossary:European_Union_(EU)|European Union]] (EU), helping to generate value added and jobs. At the same time, industrial sector activities also result in pressures on the environment such as emissions to air. This article compares the socio-economic and environmental performance of the EU's industry sector. === General overview === Between 2010 and 2023, industrial emissions of [[Glossary:Greenhouse_gas_(GHG)|greenhouse gases]] and air pollutants that damage human health and the environment decreased in the EU. At the same time, the value added generated by industry increased. Employment in the industrial sector remained stable during this period. === Industrial emissions falling despite industrial growth === Between 2010 and 2023, industrial emissions decreased (see Figure 1). The largest decrease was recorded for emissions of [[Glossary:Acidification_gas|acidifying gases]] with -61%, followed by [[Glossary:Ozone_depleting_substance_(ODS)|ozone precursor]] substances and greenhouse gas emissions with -39% and -36%, respectively. [[Glossary:Particulate_matter_-_environment|Particulates]] smaller than 2.5 µm (PM2.5) released by industrial sectors fell by -35%. During the same period, the economic value generated by industry – measured in [[Glossary:Gross_value_added|gross value added]] (GVA) – increased by 17% while [[Glossary:Employment|employment]] – measured in thousand hours worked – remained stable between 2010 and 2023, showing a small increase of 1%. [[Image:Air emissions, gross value added and employment in industry sectors (NACE B-E), EU, 2010-2023.png|thumb|centre|700px|Figure 1: Air emissions, gross value added and employment in industry sectors (NACE B-E), EU, 2010-2023
''Source:'' Eurostat ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/env_ac_ainah_r2__custom_19302679/bookmark/table?lang=en&bookmarkId=fbb11be9-9f2f-43d2-aa3e-0a49279b5d49&c=1765459912000 env_ac_ainah_r2]), ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/nama_10_a64__custom_19622934/bookmark/table?lang=en&bookmarkId=c3f72699-dd20-463f-a813-f0837daa3581&c=1768213088000 nama_10_a64_e]) ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/nama_10_a64_e__custom_19622803/bookmark/table?lang=en&bookmarkId=985b9b85-f4dc-4c93-9ced-c6bb5dffc222&c=1768212780000 nama_10_a64])|alt= Line chart showing air emissions, gross value added and employment in industry sectors (NACE B to E) in the EU. Six lines represent emissions of greenhouse gases, emissions of acidifying gases, emissions of ozone precursors, particulates, employment and gross value added over the years 2010 to 2023. The year 2010 is indexed at 100. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] === Socio-economic and environmental profile of industrial sectors === Figure 2 shows the share of industrial emissions in total production-related air emissions and presents the socio-economic and environmental profile of industrial sectors, showing how much they contribute to energy taxes, to total employment and to total GVA. [[Image:Air emissions, energy taxes, employment and gross value added in industry sectors (NACE B-E), EU, 2023.png|thumb|centre|700px|Figure 2: Air emissions, energy taxes, gross value added and employment in industry sectors (NACE B-E), EU, 2023
''Source:'' Eurostat ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/env_ac_ainah_r2__custom_19302679/bookmark/table?lang=en&bookmarkId=fbb11be9-9f2f-43d2-aa3e-0a49279b5d49&c=1765459912000 env_ac_ainah_r2]), ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/nama_10_a64_e__custom_19622803/bookmark/table?lang=en&bookmarkId=985b9b85-f4dc-4c93-9ced-c6bb5dffc222&c=1768212780000 nama_10_a64_e]), ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/nama_10_a64__custom_19622934/bookmark/table?lang=en&bookmarkId=c3f72699-dd20-463f-a813-f0837daa3581&c=1768213088000 nama_10_a64]), ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/env_ac_taxind2__custom_19625791/bookmark/table?lang=en&bookmarkId=823e915e-bedd-4cdb-9c6c-1c4e231d997c&c=1768230556000 env_ac_taxind2])|alt= Horizontal bar chart showing air emissions, energy taxes, gross value added and employment in industry sectors (NACE B to E) as percentage share in all NACE production activities in the EU. Seven bars represent emissions of greenhouse gases, emissions of acidifying gases, emissions of ozone precursors, particulates, energy taxes, employment and gross value added for the year 2023. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] In 2023, the industrial share in greenhouse gas emissions was 55%, while it was 30% for particulates smaller than 2.5 µm and 29% for ozone precursor emissions. Acidifying gases emitted by industry sectors amounted to 17% of the total acidifying emissions by production activities. In the same year, industrial sectors, relative to all NACE production activities: * generated 40% of total EU energy tax revenues * contributed 20% to total GVA in the EU economy * accounted for 16% of total EU employment (measured in hours worked) === Source data for tables and graphs === *[[Media:Industrial_emission_statistics-figures_2026-01_v1.xlsx|Download Excel file]] [[Image:Microsoft_Excel_2010_Logo.png|20px|link=]] === Data sources === This article presents data on emissions of greenhouse gases (GHG emissions), ozone precursors, acidifying gases and particulates smaller than 2.5 µm emitted by industry sectors (NACE B, C, D, E) in the EU. The main data source is Eurostat's air emissions accounts (AEAs) based on Regulation (EU) No 691/2011 on European environmental economic accounts, which are fully comparable with macroeconomic statistics. Greenhouse gases comprise carbon dioxide (CO2), nitrous oxide (N2O), methane (CH4) and fluorinated gases (hydrofluorocarbons (HFC), perfluorocarbons (PFC), sulphur hexafluoride (SF6) and natrium trifluoride (NF3). These greenhouse gases are aggregated taking into account their different capacities to cause global warming. The global warming potential (GWP) of each gas is defined in relation to a given weight of carbon dioxide (known as carbon dioxide equivalents: CO2 equivalents). The weighting factors currently used are the following: * carbon dioxide: 1; * methane: 28; * nitrous oxide: 265; * sulphur hexafluoride: 23 500. Hydrofluorocarbons and perfluorocarbons comprise a large number of different gases that have different GWPs. Acidifying gases comprise sulphur dioxide (SO2), nitrogen oxides (NOx) and ammonia (NH3). They are aggregated using respective acidifying potentials (expressed in SO2 equivalents). The following conversion factors are used: * nitrogen oxides: 0.7; * sulphur dioxide: 1.0; * ammonia: 1.9. Ozone precursors comprise non-methane volatile organic compounds (NMVOCs), nitrogen oxides (NOx), carbon monoxide (CO) and methane (CH4). They are aggregated using respective ground-level ozone forming potentials expressed in NMVOC equivalents. The following conversion factors are used: * nitrogen oxides: 1.22; * NMVOC: 1.0; * carbon monoxide: 0.11; * methane: 0.014. Particulates contain microscopic solids or liquid droplets that are so small they can be inhaled and cause serious health problems. Some particles less than 10 micrometres in diameter (PM10) can get deep into human lungs and some may even get into the bloodstream. Of these, particles less than 2.5 micrometres in diameter (PM2.5) pose the greatest risk to health. AEAs record emission data by economic activity, using the NACE classification. This arrangement enables an integrated environmental-economic analysis to be carried out in order to supplement national accounts. The scope encompasses production by all businesses resident in the country, including those operating ships, aircraft and other transportation equipment in other countries. For this article, the following NACE production activities are grouped together to denote the industry sector: * mining and quarrying – NACE section B; * manufacturing – NACE section C; * electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply – NACE section D; * water supply; sewerage, waste management and remediation activities – NACE section E. [[Glossary:Gross_value_added|Gross value added]] (GVA) is an important macroeconomic indicator derivable from [[Glossary:National_accounts_(NA)|national accounts]]. Gross value added is related to [[Glossary:Gross_domestic_product_(GDP)|gross domestic product]] (GDP). While the latter monitors economic growth at the economy-wide level, the former monitors the economic performance of individual production activities and sectors. [[Glossary:Employment|Employment]] is a significant socio-economic phenomenon. It can be measured in several ways. This article uses a volume measure expressed in [[Glossary:Hours_worked|hours actually worked]] annually. An [[Glossary:Environmental_tax|environmental tax]] is a tax whose tax base is a physical unit (or a proxy) of something that has a proven, specific negative impact on the environment and which is defined in the European System of Accounts (ESA 2010) as a tax. For analytical purposes, the environmental taxes are divided into four categories: energy taxes (including CO2 taxes), transport taxes, pollution and resource taxes. This article uses data on energy taxes. Data on environmental taxes are collected based on Regulation (EU) N° 691/2011 on European environmental economic accounts. === Context === The [https://ec.europa.eu/info/strategy/priorities-2019-2024/european-green-deal_en European Green Deal] aims to achieve [[Glossary:Sustainable_development|sustainable development]]. Assessing the sustainability of production and consumption activities requires the simultaneous monitoring of economic, social and environmental indicators. Under the heading of '[https://ec.europa.eu/environment/industry/stationary/index.htm industrial emissions]', the European Commission (Environment) lists a range of EU actions to make industry more sustainable and reduce industrial emissions. === Other Articles === *[[Greenhouse gas emission accounts|Greenhouse gas emission statistics accounts]] *[[Air_pollution_statistics_-_air_emissions_accounts|Air pollution statistics - air emissions accounts]] *[[Environmental_tax_statistics|Environmental tax statistics]] ===Database=== *[https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/environment/database Environment (env)] *[https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/environment/information-data/emissions-greenhouse-gases-air-pollutants Emissions of greenhouse gases and air pollutants], see: :Air emissions accounts (env_air_aa) ::env_ac_ainah_r2 ::env_ac_aibrid_r2 ::env_ac_aigg_q === Thematic section === *[https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/environment/overview Environment] *[https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/environment/information-data/emissions-greenhouse-gases-air-pollutants Emissions of greenhouse gases and air pollutants] ===Publications=== *{{Template:Publication|code=KS-GQ-15-009|title=Manual for air emissions accounts, 2015 edition}} ===Methodology=== *[[NACE background|NACE background]] *[https://seea.un.org/content/seea-central-framework/ System of Environmental-Economic Accounting - Central Framework] ===External links=== *[https://ec.europa.eu/environment/industry/stationary/index.htm Industrial emissions (DG Environment)] *[https://www.eea.europa.eu/ims/industrial-pollutant-releases-to-air Industrial pollutant releases to air in Europe (EEA)] {{Unit|topic=X_Environmental_accounts}} [[Category:Environment and energy|Industrial emission statistics]] [[Category:Environment|Industrial emission statistics]] [[Category:Air pollution|Industrial emission statistics]] [[Category:Statistical article|Industrial emission statistics]] [[Category:January2027|Industrial emission statistics]]

title: Industrial production statistics
text:
Data on industrial production in the EU are provided, as well as for some EFTA and candidate countries. Data extracted in August 2026 Planned article update: August 2027 In 2025, the EU’s value of sold production increased by almost 3.8% compared with 2024, amounting to nearly €6.1 trillion. This reversed the 1.8% decline recorded in 2024 and ended a two-year period of falling industrial production. [[File:Value of sold industrial production, 2015-2025.jpg |thumb|center|700px|''Source:'' Eurostat ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/d2573042-b220-4ef8-bff5-fff49d3fd2ac?lang=en&createdAt=2026-01-26T12:38:17Z DS-059358]), ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/9d76cf8a-c68e-4ef2-8aff-8b3ec523e439?lang=en&createdAt=2026-08-20T12:40:37Z DS-059367])|alt=a line chart showing the Evolution of EU's value of sold industrial production from 2015 to 2025. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] This article analyses recent data on industrial production in the [[Glossary:European Union (EU)|European Union (EU)]], based on results of [[Industrial production statistics#Context|industrial production (PRODCOM) statistics]]. Cyprus, Malta, and Luxembourg are exempt from collecting PRODCOM data and therefore no data is available. Data presented in this article are collected under the [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32020R1197 Commission Implementing Regulation] and cover the activities under sections B and C (Mining and quarrying and [[Glossary:Manufacturing|Manufacturing]]) of the [https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Glossary:NACE NACE Rev. 2.1] classification, and since 2019, the activity 38.21 Materials recovery services and secondary [[Glossary:Raw_material|raw materials]]. ===Overview=== In 2025, the value of sold production in the EU amounted to €6.1 trillion, an increase of 3.8% compared with €5.9 trillion in 2024 ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Beginners:GDP_-_Comparing_GDP:_growth_rate_and_per_capita current prices]). Figure 1 presents the evolution of the EU's value of sold production from 2015 to 2025 in [https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Beginners:Statistical_concept_-_Index_and_base_year constant prices]. After a stable period, EU production shows a constant annual increase from 2015 until 2018 when comparing to each previous year. The results of 2019 show the consolidation of the growth in production with a value of sold production in the EU that amounted to €4.9 trillion. The outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic and consequent containment measures widely introduced by countries had a significant impact on the EU's industrial production in 2020. The value of sold production in the EU in 2020 decreased by 6.6% compared with 2019. The EU's industrial production in 2021 then recovered and increased by 8.5% compared with 2020, and continued with an increase in 2022 compared with 2021 (by 0.4%). In contrast, the EU’s production of manufactured goods decreased over the next 2 consecutive years: it decreased by -1.5% in 2023 compared with 2022, and by -1.9% in 2024 compared with 2023. The recent increase observed in 2025 resulted from the growth recorded in 10 industrial activities, with the largest increase recorded in the manufacturing of motor vehicles, trailers, and semi-trailers, followed by the manufacturing of food, beverages and tobacco, and the manufacturing of computer, electronic, and optical products. In 2025, production under sub-contracted operations within the [[Glossary:Economic_territory|economic territory]] of the EU countries (available since 2021) amounted to 2.6% of the production value and 8.1% of the [[Glossary:Volume_of_industrial_production|production volume]]. [[File:Evolution_of_EU's_value_of_sold_industrial_production,_2015_-_2025_(2021=100)_.png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 1: Evolution of EU's value of sold industrial production, 2015 - 2025
''Source:'' Eurostat ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/d2573042-b220-4ef8-bff5-fff49d3fd2ac?lang=en&createdAt=2026-01-26T12:38:17Z DS-059358]), ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/9d76cf8a-c68e-4ef2-8aff-8b3ec523e439?lang=en&createdAt=2026-08-20T12:40:37Z DS-059367])|alt=a line chart showing the Evolution of EU's value of sold industrial production from 2015 to 2025. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] ===Industrial production by country=== In 2025, 6 EU countries generated 71% of the EU's value of sold production (Figure 2). Germany recorded the highest value of sold production, equivalent to 26% of the EU total, followed by Italy (14%), France (12%), Spain (8%), Poland (6%), and the Netherlands (4%). The other 21 EU countries contributed with smaller shares (4% and less). [[File:EU_value_of_sold_industrial_production,_by_country,_2025_(%_of_total_value_of_sold_production).png|thumb|center|800px|Figure 2: EU value of sold industrial production, by country, 2025
''Source:'' Eurostat ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/9d76cf8a-c68e-4ef2-8aff-8b3ec523e439?lang=en&createdAt=2026-08-20T12:44:47Z DS-059367])|alt= a pie chart showing the EU value of sold industrial production, by country in 2025. The segments show Germany, Italy, France, Spain, Poland, Netherlands, and the rest of the EU. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] Looking in detail at the 3 largest manufacturing sectors within each country in 2025: * Greece stood out with the manufacturing of food, beverages, and tobacco activities (39% of the country's total value of sold production). Spain and the Netherlands followed (each 30%), and then Croatia (28% of the country's total value of sold production). * The highest share of the total value of sold production in the manufacturing of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers, and other transport equipment was reported by Slovakia (46%), followed by Czechia (36%), Romania (30%), and Hungary (27%). * The manufacturing of basic metals and fabricated metal products generated 22% of the value of sold production in Bulgaria, 19% in Austria, Greece, and Slovenia, and 18% in Italy. In the EU, Germany was the most substantial producer of all the 3 activities mentioned above (€208 billion, €328 billion, and €200 billion, respectively). ===Industrial production by sector=== The analysis that follows refers to the division breakdown (first 2-digit level) of the statistical classification of economic activities in the European Community (NACE). In some cases, the results are presented as a group of divisions, i.e. Food, beverages, and tobacco (Divisions 10, 11 and 12 of NACE Rev. 2.1). Figure 3 shows the share of the manufacturing activities in the EU's value of sold production for 2015 and 2025 respectively. The EU's value of sold production is concentrated in 14 groups of activities; 6 of these groups account for almost three-quarters of the total for both reference years. There were 3 sectors that accounted for 47% of the value of the sold production in the EU in 2025: * The manufacture of food, beverages, and tobacco products * The manufacture of motor vehicles and other transport equipment * and the manufacture of basic metals and fabricated metal products. The value of sold production in all other manufacturing activities apart from the 6 main groups of activities increased between less than 1% and 47% in 2025 compared with 2015 (in current prices). As for the less contributing areas, the manufacture of [[Glossary:Pharmaceutical_products|pharmaceutical products]] and pharmaceutical preparations recorded the highest increase in 2025 (47%) compared to the value of sold production in 2015. Meanwhile, the production of textiles, wearing apparel, leather, and related products of other materials did not change significantly over a decade (less than 1%). [[File: Value_of_sold_production_by_group_of_manufacturing_activity,_EU,_2015_and_2025_(%_share_of_total_sold_production)_1.png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 3: Value of sold production by group of manufacturing activity, EU, 2015 and 2025
''Source:'' Eurostat ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/f8bb22d8-6ca0-49b6-aa4a-1206b9e11eed?lang=en&createdAt=2026-01-26T12:27:33Z DS-059358]), ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/9d76cf8a-c68e-4ef2-8aff-8b3ec523e439?lang=en&createdAt=2026-08-20T12:45:53Z DS-059367])|alt= two pie charts showing the value of sold production by group of manufacturing activity in the EU in 2015 and 2025. The segments show seven different manufacturing groups. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] ===The 5 largest manufacturing activities=== The analysis refers to the top 5 manufacturing activities presented at division breakdown (first 2-digit level) of the Statistical classification of economic activities in the European Community (NACE). These 5 largest manufacturing activities are: * Food products * Chemicals and chemical products * Fabricated metal products * Machinery and equipment * and motor vehicles, trailers, and semi-trailers. [[File:Evolution_of_the_value_of_sold_production_for_top_5_manufacturing_activities,_EU,_2015-2025_(2021=100).png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 4: Evolution of the value of sold production for top 5 manufacturing activities, EU, 2015-2025
''Source:'' Eurostat ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/24d1cf95-da28-45de-8ba0-8dac32e12a58?lang=en&createdAt=2026-01-26T12:21:01Z DS-059358]), ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/9d76cf8a-c68e-4ef2-8aff-8b3ec523e439?lang=en&createdAt=2026-08-20T12:46:49Z DS-059367])|alt= a line chart with 5 lines showing the evolution of the value of sold production for top 5 manufacturing activities in the EU from 2015 to 2025. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] Figure 4 shows the evolution of the value of sold production for these 5 largest manufacturing activities in the EU over [https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Beginners:Statistical_concept_-_Reference_period|the reference period] 2015-2025. Based on constant prices (base year 2021), the manufacturing of food products registered the highest increase (by 11%) in 2025 compared with 2015. It was followed by the manufacturing of machinery and equipment (by 7%) and the manufacturing of motors vehicles, trailers, and semi-trailers (by 1%). Meanwhile, the manufacturing of fabricated metal products decreased by 2% and the manufacturing of chemicals and chemical products decreased by 9%. In terms of the nominal value of sold production in 2025 compared with 2024, the manufacturing of food products went up by €52 billion, the manufacturing of machinery and equipment by €25 billion, and the manufacturing of motor vehicles, trailers, and semi-trailers by €11 billion. Meanwhile, the manufacturing of chemicals and chemical products went down by €9 billion and the manufacturing of fabricated metal products by €4 billion. ===Results for some examples of products or group of products sold=== The results are detailed at the 4-digit level of the statistical classification of economic activities in the European Community (NACE). '''Production of motor vehicles accounted for 64% of the EU's value of sold production of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers''' Figure 5 analyses the share of the value of sold production for the manufacturing of motor vehicles, trailers, and semi-trailers (Division 29 of NACE Rev. 2.1) in 2025. [[File:Sold_production_of_motor_vehicles,_trailers_and_semi-trailers,_EU,_2025.png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 5: Sold production of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers, EU, 2025
''Source:'' Eurostat ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/38445fa8-bf50-4e60-9f22-c0e4ee23e1c8?lang=en&createdAt=2026-01-26T12:29:09Z DS-059358]) ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/24bbe167-bc90-431b-a254-4def4bc692e2?lang=en&createdAt=2026-08-20T12:48:29Z DS-059367])|alt= a pie chart showing the sold production of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers in the EU in 2025. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] In 2025, the total value of sold production created by the production of motor vehicles, trailers, and semi-trailers in 2025 was €763 billion; this value represented 12.5% of the total value of sold EU production. Furthermore, the value of sold production for this manufacturing sector increased by 8% compared with 2024. The production of motor vehicles accounted for approximately €489 billion, which was more than half of the value of sold production of this group. The rest of the sold production in this activity was the production of other parts and accessories, bodies (coachwork), and electrical and electronic equipment for motor vehicles, trailers, and semi-trailers (Figure 5). '''On average, 1 kg of fresh bread produced in the EU was sold for €1.88 ''' Figure 6 presents the value of production sold for 1 kilogram (kg) of fresh bread in the EU, over the period from 2015 to 2025 and in each country for 2025. [[File:Value of sold production for 1 kg of fresh bread in the EU, 2015-2025 (EURO per kg).png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 6: Value of sold production for 1 kg of fresh bread in the EU, 2015-2025
''Source:'' Eurostat ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/69faf059-e8f0-4dd3-8a95-0a94be39357b?lang=en&createdAt=2026-01-26T16:18:35Z DS-059358]), ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/7e0aab97-cd48-4515-b588-3bd157e45efc?lang=en&createdAt=2026-08-20T12:50:53Z DS-059367])|alt= a line chart showing the value of sold production for one kilogram of fresh bread in EU from 2015 to 2025 and a vertical bar chart showing the value of sold production for one kilogram of fresh bread by country in the Member States and some candidate countries. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] Compared with the previous years, the value of fresh bread sold in the period from 2015 to 2018 remained stable. In 2019, it increased by 5% and stabilised again in 2020. In 2021, the value of sold production of this product increased significantly by 13%, in 2022 by 1%, and in 2023 by 20%. The sold value of 1 kg of fresh bread then decreased by 10% in 2024, and slightly increased by less than 1% in 2025, resulting in an EU average of a maximum of €1.88 per kg in 2025. Between 2015 and 2025, the average value of production sold for 1 kg of fresh bread increased by 21%. In the EU, Finland was the country where 1 kg of produced fresh bread was sold at the highest price, at €3.08. In Austria, Italy, and Sweden, the price ranged between €2.38 and €3.04 (per kg). Somewhat low prices, below €1 per kg, were observed in Czechia. Compared with 2024, bread prices increased in most European countries, with the highest price increases recorded in Ireland (€0.58), Belgium (€0.16), Hungary (€0.15), and Sweden (€0.14). Nine EU countries (Czechia, Italy, Germany, Latvia, Poland, Netherlands, Finland, Estonia, and Lithuania) recorded a lower price per kg of produced fresh bread in 2025 than in 2024. '''EU pharmaceutical production more than tripled in the last 10 years''' Figure 7 provides an overview of the value of total sold production of basic pharmaceutical products manufactured in the EU from 2015 to 2025. During that period, the total sold production value of pharmaceutical products fluctuated between €23.1 billion (in 2019) and €74.5 billion (in 2025). Pharmaceutical production in the EU increased due to the COVID-19 pandemic, reaching a value of €36.1 billion in 2021. Production continued to grow strongly in the years that followed, reaching €54.0 billion in 2024 and a new peak of €74.5 billion in 2025. Over the past 10 years, the production of antibiotics continued at a steady pace, with a total sold production value of €2.5 billion in 2025. The pro-vitamins and vitamins reached the highest sold production value in 2018, with the annual sold value remaining at around €2 billion from 2019 to 2025. Together, antibiotics and vitamins accounted for 6% of total basic pharmaceutical production in 2025. A large part of the recent growth recorded in “The rest of pharmaceutical products” came from hormone-based medicines, including GLP-1 medications used to treat diabetes, and increasingly, [[Glossary:Obesity|obesity]]. [[File:Sold production of basic pharmaceutical products, EU, 2015-2025 (in EURO billion).png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 7: Sold production of basic pharmaceutical products, EU, 2015-2025
''Source:'' Eurostat ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/3535773a-9db6-410b-a9fd-9a972976e018?lang=en&createdAt=2026-01-26T12:32:44Z DS-059358]), ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/ca884c3a-613f-4e49-89fa-aee55cb5410d?lang=en&createdAt=2026-08-20T12:52:18Z DS-059367])|alt=a vertical stacked bar chart showing the sold production of basic pharmaceutical products in the EU from 2015 to 2025.The bars show vitamins, antibiotics and the rest of pharmaceutical products. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] '''A look into the EU's production of wind turbines''' Figure 8 provides an overview of the number of wind turbines manufactured in the EU from 2015 to 2025. During this period, the average annual production of wind turbines was 11 200 pieces. Production fluctuated between around 8 000 and 12 000 pieces for most of this period, falling to just under 6 800 pieces in 2020. Since 2021, production has grown strongly, more than doubling from 9 100 pieces to reach a new high of 20 000 pieces in 2025. The EU main producers of wind turbines are Denmark, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Poland, Portugal, and Spain. [[File:Wind_turbines_produced_in_EU,_2015-2025_(thousand_pieces).png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 8: Wind turbines produced in EU, 2015-2025
''Source:'' Eurostat ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/e95342e7-9b2c-400f-81e7-46c5fedafd72?lang=en&createdAt=2026-01-26T12:35:07Z DS-059358]), ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/f777902f-d4a4-4be8-8892-c803048e9993?lang=en&createdAt=2026-08-20T12:53:15Z DS-059367])|alt= Vertical bar chart showing wind turbines produced in the EU from 2015 to 2025 as thousand pieces per year. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] '''Overview of sporting good production in the EU''' Figure 9 analyses the production of sporting goods from 2015 to 2025 (CPA 3230 of NACE Rev. 2.1) in the EU. The production of sporting goods in the EU increased over the past 5 years. The value of the sold production of sporting goods was at its peak with more than €4.6 billion in 2023. It then slightly decreased to €4.3 billion in 2024, before rising to a new peak of €4.8 billion in 2025. The production of these products increased mainly between 2021 and 2023, as the latest trends show a greater interest in the practice of sports worldwide. In 2021 and 2022, the sold production of fishing rods increased by 36% and 15%, respectively, compared with the average over the previous 5 years (2015 to 2020). The production of this product reached its lowest point in 2024 (€65 million), before recovering in 2025 (€88 million). Over the past 10 years, the production of winter skis increased by 42%, rising from €532 million in 2019 to €660 million in 2023. However winter skis production dropped by 24% in 2024, before rebounding by 12% to €560 million in 2025. The main producers of winter skis in the EU are Austria, Bulgaria, Czechia, France, Germany, Slovenia, and Spain. The production of tennis and badminton rackets fell by half in 2023 compared with the previous years, and significantly dropped in 2024 due to enterprises ending their production in Spain. However, production edged up slightly to €0.7 million in 2025. Conversely, gym or athletics items and equipment represented €1 billion in 2024, an increase of 28% from 2020, and continued to rise to €1.15 billion in 2025. [[File:Sporting goods produced in EU, 2015-2025 (in EURO million).png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 9: Sporting goods produced in EU, 2015-2025
''Source:'' Eurostat ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/93dd90d7-4dd2-4423-b159-40d503204844?lang=en&createdAt=2026-01-26T12:36:32Z DS-059358]), ([https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/88818bea-20c1-4174-b41c-47e120099990?lang=en&createdAt=2026-08-20T12:54:10Z DS-059367])|alt= Line chart showing sport goods produced in the EU from 2015 to 2025. Five lines represent named sports goods valued in euro millions. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] === Source data for tables and graphs === {{Template:Excel|filename=Industrial production statistics tables and figures 2025 2.xlsx|title=Industrial production statistics tables and figures}} ===Data sources=== The Prodcom list is linked to the activity classification NACE and to the [[Glossary:Statistical classification of products by activity (CPA)|classification of products by activity (CPA)]]: the first four digits of each Prodcom code refer to a NACE class, the fifth and sixth digits relate to a CPA sub-category, and the seventh and eighth digits are specific to the Prodcom list. Most headings correspond to one or more codes from the [[Glossary:Combined nomenclature (CN)|combined nomenclature (CN)]], a classification used for statistics on international trade in goods: some headings (mostly industrial services) do not correspond to a CN heading at all. The relationship with CN makes it possible to calculate apparent consumption by linking production statistics to international trade statistics. The production surveyed covers only the production actually carried out on the territory of the reporting country. This means that the production of subsidiaries, which takes place outside an enterprise's territory, is not included in the survey results for that country. As a general principle, when a production process takes as an input a material that does not match the description of the product, and produces as an output something that does, then production of the product should be recorded. If the processing of a product does not change the heading under which it is listed, it should not be recorded, since this would result in double-counting. This means that the link to turnover data is tenuous, since some activities do not result in new products and should not be recorded in Prodcom statistics. Prodcom data are available for the EU Member States, Iceland, Norway, Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, and Serbia; [[Glossary:Eurostat|Eurostat]] produces aggregates for the EU. According to the terms of the {{Template:EurLex|code=CONSLEG:1991R3924:20080101:EN:PDF|title=Prodcom Regulation}}, Cyprus, Luxembourg, and Malta have derogations not to provide Prodcom data to Eurostat because of their size; as such there is no data for these 3 Member States in the database. Data are available during the year following the reference year, with the [[Glossary:First_release|first release]] of information usually taking place in July. As more complete and revised data become available, updates are released on a monthly basis. ===Context=== The development of Prodcom dates back to 1985 when Eurostat organised a series of meetings on production statistics, whose objective was to harmonise the various ways industrial production statistics were collected in the EU Member States. Although statistics were collected on products in most countries, there was a varied selection of classifications in use reflecting national situations and a range of different survey methods were applied. The Prodcom Regulation is designed to enable these national statistics to be compared and, where possible, [[Glossary:Aggregate|aggregated]] to give a picture of the developments of an industry or product in the European context. This aim became more urgent with the creation of the [[Glossary:Single market|single market]] in 1992 and the statistical system had to adapt. Before data collection could begin, it was necessary to draw up a common list of products to be covered. Drawing up the Prodcom list was a unique opportunity for Eurostat, the national statistical authorities, and the European trade associations to work together to produce a classification that would be understood by businesses and would be appropriate for national and European statistics. Industrial production statistics collected within PRODCOM serves as one of the data sources used in several policy areas of the [[Glossary:European Commission (EC)|European Commission]] and national administrations. Other users such as professional/trade associations and their members use PRODCOM statistics for information on industry. The use of the data in [[Glossary:Climate_change|climate change]] statistics is increasing, as well as in other environmental statistics such as the analysis of [[Material_flow_accounts_-_flows_in_raw_material_equivalents|material flows]] or [[Chemicals production and consumption statistics|chemicals production and consumption statistics]]. ===Other articles=== *[[Business economy by sector - NACE Rev. 2]] (online publication) *[[Chemicals production and consumption statistics]] *[[Material flow accounts and resource productivity]] ===Database=== *[https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/prodcom/database Prodcom - statistics by product (prom)], see: :Sold production, exports and imports by PRODCOM list (CPA 2.2) - annual data (DS_059367) :Total production by PRODCOM list (CPA 2.2) - annual data (DS_059368) :Sold production, exports and imports - annual data (DS_059358) :Total production - annual data (DS_059359) :Traditional international trade database access (Comext) (comext) === Thematic section === *[https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/prodcom/overview Manufactured goods — Prodcom] ===Methodology=== *{{Template:Esms|code=prom_esms|title=Statistics on the production of manufactured goods}} (ESMS metadata file — prom_esms) *[https://op.europa.eu/en/web/eu-vocabularies/eurostat Eurostat - EU Vocabularies - Publications Office of the EU] (PRODCOM List) ===Legislation=== *[https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/prodcom/legislation Legislation - PRODCOM - statistics by product - Eurostat] {{Unit|topic=X_PRODCOM}} [[Category:Industry, trade, and services|Industrial production statistics]] [[Category:Manufactured goods (Prodcom)|Industrial production statistics]] [[Category:Industrial production|Industrial production statistics]] [[Category:Industry and construction|Industrial production statistics]] [[Category:Industry|Industrial production statistics]] [[Category:Manufacturing|Industrial production statistics]] [[Category:Statistical_article|Industrial production statistics]] [[Category:Production statistics|Industrial production statistics]] [[Category:August2027|Industrial production statistics]]
