title: Tourism statistics
text:
EU tourism statistics cover various aspects: tourism trips, offer in accommodation establishments, tourism receipts and employment, the most popular destinations... Data extracted in March 2026 Planned article update: February 2027 65% of EU residents made at least one personal tourism trip in 2024. 7 out of 10 trips by European tourists in 2024 were spent in their own country. In 2024, Spain was again the most visited tourism destination in the EU for international tourists, with 322 million nights spent in tourist accommodation establishments. This article provides a general introduction to statistics on [[Glossary:Tourism|tourism]] in the [[Glossary:European Union (EU)|European Union (EU)]]. The data shown here are discussed in more detail in [[:Category:Tourism|several other articles]].
Tourism plays an important role in the EU because of its economic and employment potential, as well as its social and environmental implications. [[Glossary:European statistics on tourism|Tourism statistics]] are not only used to monitor the tourism policies across the EU but also regional and [[Glossary:Sustainable development|sustainable development]] policies.
The first part of the article takes a look at domestic and foreign tourism by EU residents, the second part looks at inbound and domestic tourism in the EU using accommodation data, while a third part focuses on tourism expenditure and the economic value of tourism. === Tourism participation: 65% of EU residents made at least one personal trip=== '''More than 3 out of 4 residents of the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Finland, Sweden, France, Germany, Ireland, Austria and Czechia participated in tourism'''
In 2024, 65% of the EU population aged 15 or over took part in tourism for personal purposes, in other words they made at least one tourism trip for personal purposes with at least one overnight stay during the year (such as holidays, leisure, visiting friends and relatives). However, large differences can be observed between the [[Glossary:EU_Member_States|EU countries]], as this participation rate ranged from 27.7% in Romania to 83.6% in the Netherlands (see Figure 1 and Table 1). Figure 1 More information can be found in the article: [[Tourism statistics - participation in tourism|Tourism statistics - participation in tourism]] === Tourism trips: 7 EU countries made more foreign than domestic trips === '''71% of all trips made by EU residents were inside their own country'''
EU [[Glossary:Country_of_residence|residents]] (aged 15 and above) made 1.2 billion tourism trips in 2024, either for personal or business purposes. Residents of Luxembourg, Belgium, Malta, Slovenia, Austria, the Netherlands and Cyprus made more foreign than domestic trips. The number of trips increased by 4% compared with 2023 and by 67% compared with 2020. Compared with the pre-pandemic year 2019, tourism by Europeans has fully recovered, with the number of trips being 5% higher in 2024. More than half (56%) of these trips were [[Glossary:Tourism trip length|short trips]] of 1 to 3 nights (see Table 1). Around 71% of all trips made were to domestic destinations, while 29% were to destinations abroad. [[Image:T1_Tourism trips of Europeans (aged 15 years or more), 2024_v2.png|thumb|centre|700px|Table 1: Tourism trips of Europeans, 2024
''Source:'' Eurostat [https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/5f141d48-87fd-4023-b7c5-42e24010b9b8?lang=en&createdAt=2026-04-08T08:34:21Z tour_dem_tttot], [https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/7136185f-c5c2-4dc8-a727-53f709c6f9ab?lang=en&createdAt=2026-04-08T08:35:20Z tour_dem_totot]|alt= Table showing tourism trips of Europeans aged 15 years and over in thousands of trips, percentage destination type and duration and percentage share of population in the EU and individual EU Member States for the year 2024. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] Notwithstanding the dominance of domestic trips, residents of 7 EU countries mainly visited foreign countries. In 2024, 95.3% of the total number of tourism trips made by residents of Luxembourg were to destinations abroad, followed by Belgians with 76.8%, residents of Malta (64.5%), Slovenia (58.1%), Austria (52.4%), the Netherlands (52.1%) and Cyprus (51.9%). However, only 1 of 10 trips taken by residents of Romania (10.4%) were abroad. These figures appear to be influenced by both the size of the EU countries and their geographical location (smaller and more northerly countries tended to report a higher propensity for their residents to travel abroad).
In 2024, EU residents showed a preference to travel in the summer months with one third of their trips made in July or August. More information can be found in the publication: [[Tourism trips of Europeans|Tourism trips of Europeans (online publication)]] ===Nights spent abroad by EU residents === '''Residents of Germany, France and the Netherlands accounted for more than half of the total number of nights spent abroad by EU residents in 2024''' EU residents spent an estimated 2.7 billion nights during 343 million tourism trips abroad in 2024 (see Figure 2). German residents spent 978 million nights on trips outside of Germany in 2024, while residents of France and the Netherlands spent respectively 238 million and 225 million nights abroad; residents from these 3 EU countries accounted for more than half (54.1%) of the total number of nights spent abroad by EU residents. Luxembourg leads in nights per inhabitant. Figure 2 When taking into account a country’s population, Luxembourg had the highest number of nights spent abroad per inhabitnt among all EU countries (an average of 38 nights in 2024), followed by Sweden (with 18 nights spent abroad per inhabitant) and Cyprus (with 16 nights spent abroad per inhabitant). At the other end of the spectrum, residents of Romania, Greece, Bulgaria, Italy and Portugal spent, on average, less than 3 nights abroad in 2024 (see Figure 3). Figure 3 More information can be found in the online publication: [[Tourism trips of Europeans|Tourism trips of Europeans]] === Tourism accommodation establishments in the EU: Italy and Croatia predominate === ''' In 2024, more than one third of all bed places in the EU were in Italy or France ''' It is estimated that there were more than 680 000 [[Glossary:Tourist accommodation establishment|tourist accommodation establishments]] active within the EU in 2024 and together these provided 29.7 million [[Glossary:Bed places|bed places]] (see Table 2). More than one third (35.5%) of all the bed places in the EU were concentrated in just 2 of the EU countries, namely Italy (5.5 million) and France (5.1 million), while more than half (57.0%) of all the establishments in the EU were concentrated in Italy (265 000), and Croatia (122 000). Note that comparability of the number of establishments may be affected by differences in registration schemes or obligations across Europe. [[Image:T2_Tourist_accommodation_establishments,_2024_v2.png|thumb|centre|700px|Table 2: Tourist accommodation establishments, 2024
''Source:'' Eurostat [https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/b3956056-e0d1-4fa7-a425-f3392bc89c30?lang=en&createdAt=2026-03-12T15:25:01Z tour_cap_nat], [https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/5dea9728-e4d7-478b-8087-81033fcaa9e3?lang=en&createdAt=2026-03-12T14:15:50Z tour_occ_ninat], [https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/36a273a8-9cb0-49c8-9e05-98562b3adb6a?lang=en&createdAt=2026-03-12T14:20:30Z tour_occ_nim]|alt= Table showing tourist accommodation establishments in the EU, individual EU Member States, EFTA countries, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Albania, Serbia, Türkiye and Kosovo for the year 2024. Shown are number of establishments in units, number of bed places in thousands and total nights spent in millions. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] More information can be found in the article: [[Tourism statistics - annual results for the accommodation sector|Tourism statistics - annual results for the accommodation sector]] ===Spain remains the top EU destination for international tourists=== '''Nearly half of nights spent by international guests in the EU were spent in Spain, Italy and France''' In 2024, the number of [[Glossary:Nights spent|nights spent]] at EU tourist accommodation establishments was 7.0% higher and the number of bedplaces was 1.8% higher than in the same period last year. The number of nights spent by foreign tourists increased more significantly (+57.6%) than domestic tourists (+26.3%) from the base year 2010 (see Figure 4). Figure 4 In 2024, Spain was the most visited tourism destination in the EU for international tourists (people travelling outside their country), with 322 million nights spent in tourist accommodation establishments, or 22.2% of the EU total (see Figure 5 and Figure 6). In 2024, the top 5 [[Glossary:Nomenclature of territorial units for statistics (NUTS)|NUTS 3 regions]] in the EU were Mallorca, Roma, Barcelona, Tenerife and Venezia. These 5 regions jointly accounted for 12% of nights spent by foreign tourists in the EU. The second most popular EU destination for international tourists in 2024 was Italy (254 million nights), followed by France (141 million nights), Greece (128 million nights) and Austria (94 million nights). These 5 countries together accounted for nearly two thirds (64.7%) of the total nights spent by non-residents in the EU. On the other hand, the least common EU destinations in terms of nights spent, were the relatively smaller countries Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg and Estonia, with less than 4 million nights spent by international tourists in each of these countries. Figure 5
Figure 6 The number of total nights spent (by domestic and international guests) can be put into perspective by making a comparison with the country’s population, providing an indicator of [[Glossary:Tourism intensity|tourism intensity]]. In 2024, using this measure, the Mediterranean destinations of Croatia (24 nights spent per inhabitant), Malta (20 nights spent per inhabitant) and Cyprus (19 nights spent per inhabitant) were ahead (see Figure 7), followed by Greece (15 nights spent per inhabitant) and Austria (14 nights spent per inhabitant). The tourism intensity becomes more pronounced when looking at the peak months or at popular tourism regions. Figure 7 More information can be found in the following articles: *[[Tourism statistics - annual results for the accommodation sector|Tourism statistics - annual results for the accommodation sector]] *[[Tourism statistics - nights spent at tourist accommodation establishments|Tourism statistics - nights spent at tourist accommodation establishments]] (this article uses monthly data and shows the most recent information, including data for all months of 2025, albeit with less detail in terms of origin of the tourists) *[[Tourism statistics - seasonality at regional level|Tourism statistics - seasonality at regional level]] *[[Seasonality in the tourist accommodation sector|Seasonality in the tourist accommodation sector]] *[[Tourism statistics at regional level|Tourism statistics at regional level]] ===Over 950 million short-stay guest nights booked via Airbnb, Booking and Expedia=== The data presented in the previous sections comes from accommodation statistics collected from service providers in the accommodation sector (such as hotels, campsites or other short-stay accommodation). Since 2020, Eurostat also publishes data on short-term rentals booked via Airbnb, Booking and Expedia, based on data sharing agreements with these 3 platforms. These statistics give relevant stand-alone information on this particular segment of the tourist accommodation market. It should be noted that these figures are not necessarily additive to the traditional accommodation statistics shown above, as some service providers that put their accommodation offer on the platforms may also report data on their occupancy to the statistical authorities. In 2025, a total of 951.6 million short-stay guest nights were booked via Airbnb, Booking and Expedia, representing an 11.4% increase compared with 2024. Figure 8 More information can be found in the following articles: *[[Short-stay_accommodation_offered_via_online_collaborative_economy_platforms_-_monthly_data|Short-stay accommodation offered via online collaborative economy platforms – monthly data]] *[[Short-stay_accommodation_offered_via_online_collaborative_economy_platforms| Short-stay accommodation offered via online collaborative economy platforms]] ===Tourism expenditure: highest spending by German residents=== '''Germans were the biggest EU spenders on international travel, totalling €115 billion in 2024''' The economic importance of international tourism can be measured by looking at the ratio of international travel receipts relative to GDP; these data are from balance of payments statistics and include business travel, as well as travel for pleasure. In 2024, the ratio of travel receipts to GDP was highest, among the EU countries, in Croatia (17.5%), Cyprus and Malta (10.6% each), Portugal (9.6%) and Greece (9.1%), confirming the importance of inbound tourism to these countries (see Table 3). In absolute terms, the highest international travel receipts in 2024 were recorded in Spain (€98 billion), followed by France (€71 billion), Italy (€54 billion) and Germany (€38 billion). [[Image:T3 Travel receipts and expenditure in balance of payments, 2010-2015-2024 data.png|thumb|centre|700px|Table 3: Travel receipts and expenditure in balance of payments, 2010-2015-2024
''Source:'' Eurostat [https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/5a1bc427-27cd-41ea-bf13-f0bfc0f8d745?lang=en&createdAt=2026-04-13T13:11:05Z bop_c6_q], [https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/11d12633-4bf8-40a0-9651-550a08dd5d07?lang=en&createdAt=2026-04-13T13:07:41Z bop_eu6_q], [https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/bf71590f-f29f-49cb-82f9-2827e33fc93e?lang=en&createdAt=2026-04-13T12:59:05Z nama_10_gdp], [https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/86d1f93a-86d3-45ca-b89b-ee9834ea974d?lang=en&createdAt=2026-04-13T13:06:57Z demo_pjan]|alt= Table showing travel receipts and expenditure in balance of payments as millions euro and percentage relative to GDP of receipts, expenditure and balance of the EU, individual EU Member States, Iceland, Norway, Switzerland, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Albania, Serbia, Türkiye and Kosovo for the years 2010, 2015 and 2024. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] Germany recorded the highest level of expenditure on international travel, totalling €115 billion in 2024, followed by France (€55 billion). When analysing this expenditure relative to the population, Luxembourg's residents spent on average €7 638 per inhabitant on travel abroad in 2024, far ahead of the second and third ranked countries, Ireland and Belgium (€2 443 and €2 099 per inhabitant respectively), which were followed by Cyprus, Denmark, Austria, the Netherlands, Germany, Sweden, Slovenia, Malta, Finland and Estonia (all above €1 000 per inhabitant). Spain was the EU country with the highest level of net receipts from travel in 2024 (€68 billion), while Germany recorded the biggest deficit (-€77 billion). More information can be found in the following articles: *[[International_trade_in_services_by_type_of_service|International trade in services by type of service]] *[[Tourism statistics - expenditure|Tourism statistics - expenditure]] === Tourism accounted for 3.6 % of the total gross value added in the EU economy=== To understand the economic dimension of tourism and the sector’s impact on the economy and on the labour market, the methodological framework of Tourism Satellite Accounts (TSA) was developed. Currently, data on TSA for Europe are only available as experimental statistics (but in some EU countries TSA are part of the regularly produced tourism statistics). A main indicator from TSA is the tourism direct gross value added. Figure 9 shows the share of tourism direct gross value added in the total gross value added in the entire economy, giving an indication of the macro-economic importance of tourism. On average for the EU, tourism accounted for 3.6 % of the gross value added created in the EU during 2022, which was well below the pre-pandemic level (estimated at 4.5% for 2019) and indicating the EU tourism sector was still recovering from the pandemic in 2022. Large variations can be observed across the EU: from 10.5 % in Croatia to 0.8 % in Luxembourg (note that data was not available for Bulgaria, Cyprus, Estonia, Greece, Ireland, Latvia and Malta). In absolute value, tourism direct gross value added amounted to €517 billion in 2022. The main contributors to this estimate at EU level, were the tourism sector from Germany (€92 billion), France (€82 billion) and Spain (€75 billion) (note that for Italy no comparable data for 2022 is available). The gross value added is not only created via trips spent in a country, but for instance also by resident service providers (such as airlines or tour operators) that provide tourism services to residents visiting destinations abroad. Figure 9 More information can be found in the following articles: *[[Tourism satellite accounts on Europe|Tourism satellite accounts on Europe]] *[https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-statistical-reports/w/ks-01-26-018 Tourism Satellite Accounts in Europe – 2026 edition] === Source data for tables === *{{Template:Excel|filename=Tourism statistics_2024 data tables.xlsx|title=Tourism statistics: tables}} ===Data sources=== Tourism, in a statistical context, refers to the activity of visitors taking a trip to a destination outside their usual environment, for less than a year. It can be for any main purpose, including business, leisure or other personal reasons other than to be employed by a resident person, [[Glossary:Household|household]] or [[Glossary:Enterprise|enterprise]] in the place visited. In July 2011, the [[Glossary:European Parliament (EP)|European Parliament]] and the [[Glossary:Council of the European Union|Council of the European Union]] adopted {{Template:EurLex|code=CELEX:32011R0692:EN:NOT|title=Regulation (EU) No 692/2011}} concerning European statistics on tourism and repealing {{Template:EurLex|code=CELEX:31995L0057:EN:NOT|title=Council Directive 95/57/EC}}; requiring EU Member States to provide a regular set of comparable tourism statistics. Tourism statistics in the EU consist of 2 main components: on the one hand, statistics relating to capacity and occupancy of collective tourist accommodation; on the other, statistics relating to tourism demand. In most EU Member States, the former are collected via surveys filled in by accommodation establishments, while the latter are mainly collected via traveller surveys at border crossings or through household surveys. Statistics on the capacity of collective tourist accommodation include the number of establishments, the number of bedrooms and the number of bed places. These statistics are available by establishment type or by region and are compiled annually. Statistics on the occupancy of collective tourist accommodation refer to the number of arrivals (at accommodation establishments) and the number of [[Glossary:Nights spent|nights spent]] by residents and non-residents, separated into establishment type or region; annual and monthly statistical series are available. In addition, statistics on the use of bedrooms and bed places ([[Glossary:Net occupancy rate|occupancy rates]]) are compiled. From the reference year 2018 onwards, Eurostat also publishes, as separate series, data on occupancy of short-term rentals booked via Airbnb, Booking or Expedia Group. Statistics on tourism demand are collected in relation to the number of tourism trips made (and the number of nights spent on those trips), separated by: :*destination country; :*purpose; :*length of stay; :*accommodation type; :*departure month; :*transport mode; :*expenditure. The data are also analysed by the socio-demographic characteristics of the tourist: :*sex; :*age group; :*educational attainment level (optional); :*household income (optional); :*activity status (optional). Data from a range of other official sources may be used to study tourism. These statistics include: :*[[Glossary:Structural business statistics (SBS)|structural business statistics (SBS)]] and [[Glossary:Short-term business statistics|short-term business statistics (STS)]] which may be used to provide additional information on tourism flows and on the economic performance of certain tourism-related sectors; :*[[Tourism_industries_-_economic_analysis|tourism industries – economic analysis]] :*data on employment in the tourism accommodation sector from the [[Glossary:Labour force survey (LFS)|labour force survey (LFS)]], analysed by working time (full/part-time), working status, age, level of education, sex, permanency and seniority of work with the same employer (annual and quarterly data); :*[[Tourism_industries_-_employment|tourism industries - employment]] :*data on personal travel receipts and expenditure from the [[Glossary:Balance of payments|balance of payments]]; :*[[Transport|transport statistics]] (for example, air passenger transport). ===Context=== According to a UN Tourism (formerly UNWTO) publication titled [https://www.e-unwto.org/doi/book/10.18111/9789284425808 International Tourism Highlights 2024], the EU is a major tourist destination, with 4 of its Member States among the world’s top 10 destinations. Tourism has the potential to contribute towards employment and economic growth, as well as to development in rural, peripheral or less-developed areas. These characteristics drive the demand for reliable and harmonised statistics within this field, as well as within the wider context of regional policy and sustainable development policy areas. Tourism can play a significant role in the development of European regions. Infrastructure created for tourism purposes contributes to local development, while jobs that are created or maintained can help counteract industrial or rural decline. Sustainable tourism involves the preservation and enhancement of cultural and natural heritage, ranging from the arts to local gastronomy or the preservation of [[Glossary:Biodiversity|biodiversity]]. ===Other articles=== *[[:Category:Tourism|All articles on tourism statistics]] *[[Tourism trips of Europeans]] (online publication) ===Publications=== *[http://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/tourism/publications Recent Eurostat publications on tourism] ===Database=== *[https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/tourism/database Tourism (tour)] *Tourism [https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/main/data/database?node_code=t_tour (t_tour)] ===Thematic section=== *[{{Template:Dedicated section|dedicated_section=tourism}} Tourism] ===Methodology=== *{{Template:Esms|code=tour_dem_esms|title=Trips of EU residents - annual data}} (ESMS metadata file — tour_dem_esms) *{{Template:Esms|code=tour_occ_esms|title=Capacity and occupancy of tourist accommodation establishments}} (ESMS metadata file — tour_occ_esms) *{{Template:Publication|code=KS-GQ-13-007|title=Methodological manual for tourism statistics}} ===Legislation=== *{{Template:EurLex|code=CELEX:52007DC0621:EN:NOT|title=Agenda for a sustainable and competitive European tourism}} (Communication from the European Commission, October 2007) ===External links=== *[https://transport.ec.europa.eu/tourism_en Tourism, Mobility and Transport] - European Commission — Directorate-General (DG) for Mobility and Transport ''View this article online at http://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php/Tourism_statistics'' {{Unit|topic=X_Tourism}} [[Category:Industry, trade, and services|Tourism statistics]] [[Category:Tourism|Tourism statistics]] [[Category:Vistool|Tourism statistics]] [[Category:Statistical_article|Tourism statistics]] [[Category:February2027|Tourism statistics]]

title: Tourism statistics - characteristics of tourism trips
text:
Statistics on the characteristics of trips made by EU residents. Data extracted in October 2025 Planned article update: November 2026 EU residents made 1.2 billion trips with overnight stays in 2024. In 2024, EU residents spent 92% of their tourism trips inside the European Union. In 2024, EU residents made over 123 million business trips, representing 10% of the total number of tourism trips. |alt= Dynamic a line chart showing the tourism trends from 2007 to 2024. There are 4 lines and they show personal trips, business trips, personal nights, business nights. This article is part of the [[Glossary:Eurostat|Eurostat]] online publication '''[[Tourism trips of Europeans]]''' providing statistics on tourism [[Glossary:Demand side tourism statistics|demand]] in the [[Glossary:European Union (EU)|European Union (EU)]] and [[Glossary:EFTA|EFTA]] countries. The article takes a closer look at trips that EU residents (aged 15 years and over) made in 2024, with a focus on the characteristics of these trips. Specific aspects such as [[Tourism_statistics_-_top_destinations|top destinations]], [[Seasonality_in_tourism_demand|seasonality]] and [[Tourism_statistics_-_expenditure|expenditure]] on tourism trips are dealt with in more detail elsewhere in other articles of this publication. This article concentrates on analysis for the European Union at aggregate level. More detailed information at country level is available in the [https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/tourism/database online database]. ===General overview=== During 2024, EU residents made nearly 1.2 billion trips with overnight stays - regardless of destination and duration (see Table 1). During these trips, almost 6 billion tourism nights were spent. Of these trips, 10.3% were trips for professional purposes, while the remaining 89.7% were trips made for personal purposes (see Figure 1). The highest number of trips was made by residents of Germany (277 million trips), followed by France (240 million trips) and Spain (149 million trips). The trips made by the residents of these 3 countries accounted for more than half (55.9%) of all EU residents' trips. [[Image:T1_Trips, nights spent and average length of trips made by EU residents by destination, 2024.png|thumb|centre|800px|Table 1: Trips, nights spent and average length of trips made by EU residents by destination, 2024
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_tttot}}, {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_tntot}}|alt= a table showing the Trips, nights spent and average length of trips made by EU residents by destination in 2024 in the EU and EU countries. The columns show the number of trips, domestic and foreign, the number of nights, domestic and foreign and the average length of trips, domestic and foreign. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] On average for the EU, nearly 3 out of 4 (71.3%) trips were domestic trips, while over half of the tourism nights were spend on domestic territory (55.3%). The highest number of domestic trips was in France, with 204 million accounting for 24% of all domestic trips made by Europeans. As regards foreign trips, German tourists came on top, with over 114 million foreign trips (33% of all foreign trips made by Europeans). Eight out of 10 trips made by residents of Romania, Spain, France, Portugal and Greece had a main destination inside their own country. In 7 EU countries foreign trips accounted for more than half of all tourism trips: Luxembourg (95.3%), Belgium (76.8%), Malta (64.5%), Slovenia (58.1%), Austria (52.4%), the Netherlands (52.1%) and Cyprus (51.9%). === Only 1 in 10 trips was for professional purposes === More than half of the tourism trips (53.2%) had holidays, leisure and recreation as the main purpose, and almost 1 out of every 3 trips (31.6%) were to visit relatives and friends. The latter accounted for a big share of short trips and of domestic trips (see Figure 1). In total, including other purposes such as pilgrimages or health treatment, trips for personal purposes made up 89.7% of all tourism trips in 2024. In 2024, EU residents made over 123 million trips for professional purposes (e.g. business trips), representing 10.3% of the total number of tourism trips. Most of these trips were domestic (72.1%) and had a duration of maximum 3 nights (75.6%). [[Image:F1_Trips made by EU residents by purpose, duration and destination, 2024 (million).png|thumb|centre|700px|Figure 1: Trips made by EU residents by purpose, duration and destination, 2024 (million)
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_ttpur}}|alt= A vertical stacked bar chart showing Trips made by EU residents by purpose, duration and destination in 2024. The bars show all trips, from 1-3 nights, 4 nights or over, domestic and foreign and the stacks on each bar show the purpose of holidays, leisure and recreation; visits to relatives and friends; other personal and professional, business. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] === Europeans spend on average 5 nights during tourism trips === Τourism trips made during the course of 2024 were dominated by short domestic breaks of 1 to 3 overnight stays (48.0% of all tourism trips, see Table 2). Trips of 4 nights or more accounted for 43.7% of all tourism trips (23.3% with a domestic destination and 20.4% with a destination outside the country of residence). The average length of nights spent by the EU residents on a trip was of 3.9 nights during domestic trips and 7.8 nights during foreign trips. The highest average length of stay during domestic trips was recorded by residents in Greece (10.0 nights), while for foreign trips by residents from the Netherlands (9.1 nights) (see Table 1). [[Image:T2_Trips of EU residents by duration and destination, 2024.png|thumb|centre|800px|Table 2: Trips of EU residents by duration and destination, 2024
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_ttw}}|alt= a table showing the Trips of EU residents by duration and destination in 2024 in the EU and EU countries. The columns show the number of trips and the share by duration and destination. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] === The EU is an attractive destination for its residents === More than 2 out of 3 foreign trips had as main destination another EU country, accounting for 250 million trips out of a total of 343 million foreign trips. Taking into account the 850 million domestic trips, this means that 92.2% of all trips with overnight stays that EU residents made in 2024 were within the European Union. Even when restricting the analysis to longer trips of at least 4 overnight stays – more likely to be further away from home – 85.8% were spent within the EU. Only in 3 EU countries was the share of trips outside the EU more than 15%: Ireland (19.5%), Luxembourg (17.3%) and Malta (16.7%)(see Table 2). There is more detailed information on the destinations EU residents chose for their trips in a [[Tourism statistics - top destinations|separate article]]. === 84% of all trips made in 2024 lasted a maximum of 1 week === In 2024, 56.3% of the tourism trips that EU residents made were short, taking a maximum of 3 overnight stays (see Table 2 and Figure 2). More than 2 out of 3 trips made by residents of Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Finland and Spain were short trips. In 7 EU countries, the number of long trips exceeded the number of short trips: Greece (74.6%), Belgium (61.2%), Luxembourg (58.9%), Italy (58.2%), Germany (52.2%), the Netherlands (51.3%) and Malta (51.0%). [[Image:F2_Trips made by EU residents by duration, 2024 (million).png|thumb|centre|700px|Figure 2: Trips made by EU residents by duration, 2024
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_ttls}}|alt= a horizontal bar chart showing Trips made by EU residents by duration in 2024. The bars show the duration. 1 night, 2 nights, 3 nights, 4-7 nights, 8-14 nights, 15-28 nights, 29-91 nights, and 92 nights or more. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] The share of trips that lasted a maximum of 1 week was obtained by adding the short trips of 1 to 3 nights (56.3%) with the trips lasting 4 to 7 nights (27.7%), resulting in a dominant share of 84.0% of all trips made in 2024 (if we consider only trips for professional purposes this share was 94.5%). While only 9.6% of the domestic trips were longer than 1 week, this was the case for 32.0% of the trips abroad. Only 5.2% of all trips were longer than 2 weeks (see Table 3). [[Image:T3_Trips made by EU residents by duration, destination and purpose, 2024.png|thumb|centre|800px|Table 3: Trips made by EU residents by duration, destination and purpose, 2024
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_ttls}}|alt= a table showing the Trips made by EU residents by duration, destination and purpose in 2024. The table shows the number of trips and the length of stay as a percentage of total. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] === Over half of all overnight stays were in rented accommodation === EU residents made a total of 6 billion overnight stays during tourism trips in 2024 (see Table 1). More than half of these nights (58.2%) were spent in rented accommodation, while 41.8% were spent in non-rented accommodation (see Figure 3). Hotels or similar accommodation providing services such as daily cleaning and bed-making came on top with 31.2%, followed by accommodation provided without charge by relatives or friends with 27.3%, while 16.9% were spent at a rented house, villa, apartment or rented room(s) in a dwelling. Rented accommodation was more prevalent for foreign trips (72.0%), while tourists travelling within their own country were more likely to stay at non-rented accommodation (52.9%), provided mainly for free by friends or relatives (34.3%). [[Image:F3_Nights spent by EU residents by main means of accommodation, 2024.png|thumb|centre|700px|Figure 3: Nights spent by EU residents by main means of accommodation, 2024
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_tnac}}|alt= Three pie charts showing the Nights spent by EU residents by main means of accommodation in 2024. One pie chart shows all trips, the second, domestic trips and the third, foreign trips. The segments on each pie chart show rented accommodation – hotels and similar, campsites, caravans or trailer parks, house, villa, apartment or rented room(s) in a dwelling and other; and non-rented accommodation – own holiday home, provided without charge by relatives or friends and other. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] Looking only at nights spent in rented accommodation, in 2024 EU residents spent more than half of these tourism nights (53.5%) in hotels (or similar), close to 2014 level (54.5%). More than 1 out of 3 nights (37.0%) were spent in rented accommodation other than hotels or campsites (see Figure 4). As seen in Figure 5, the segment of rented accommodation recorded an increase compared with 2014 (growth of 25.1%), with the highest increase recorded for the category other than hotels or campsites (+32.8%). This latter category includes, among others, holiday dwellings, rented rooms in family houses and [[Short-stay_accommodation_offered_via_online_collaborative_economy_platforms|short-stay accommodation offered via online collaborative economy platforms]]. The increase in hotels or similar accommodation was also consistent, with +22.9% in 2024 compared to a decade ago, while the number of tourism nights spent by EU residents in campsites, caravans or trailer parks increased with +11.5% in the past 10 years. Non-rented accommodation decreased by -1.6% because of the drop in non-rented accommodation provided without charge by relatives or friends (-6.6%) which represents around 2 thirds of the total non-rented accommodation. The other 2 categories had an increase in 2024 compared to 2014: own holiday home (+7.0%) and other (+22.6%), which is a small segmented of tourist accommodation. In 2024, EU residents spent an estimated EUR 215 billion on tourist accommodation (for more detailed information on tourism expenditure, see [[Tourism statistics - expenditure|separate article]]). [[Image:F4_Distribution of tourism nights spent in rented accommodation by EU residents, by mode of accommodation, 2014-2024 (%).png|thumb|centre|700px|Figure 4: Distribution of tourism nights spent in rented accommodation by EU residents, by mode of accommodation, 2014-2024
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_tnac}}|alt= two pie charts showing the Distribution of tourism nights spent in rented accommodation by EU residents, by mode of accommodation, 2014 and 2024. The pie charts represent the years 2014 and 2024 and the segments show the different types of rented accommodation, hotels and similar, campsites, caravans or trailer parks, other. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]]
[[Image:F5_Change in the number of tourism nights of EU residents, by mode of accommodation (% change 2014-2024).png|thumb|centre|700px|Figure 5: Change in the number of tourism nights of EU residents, by mode of accommodation
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_tnac}}|alt= column chart showing the Change in the number of tourism nights of EU residents, by mode of accommodation, in % change between 2014-2024. The columns show the different types of rented accommodation – total, hotels and similar, campsites, caravans or trailer parks, other and non-rented accommodation – total, own holiday home, provided without charge by relatives or friends and other. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] === More than 1 in 8 trips of Europeans were made by train === Motor vehicles (private or rented) were the main means of transport for 64.1% of all trips, followed by air transport and railway (16.2% and 13.2%, respectively) (see Figure 6). Other modes of transport were relatively insignificant, though it is important to note that this pattern can be very different at country level. Waterways were the main means of transport for 42.2% of trips made by residents of Malta and 16.2% of trips made by Greek residents, while residents of Bulgaria, Estonia and Romania took buses for more than 10% of their trips (see Table 4). Motor vehicles were the preferred means of transport for domestic trips (75.2%), followed by rail (16.1%) and bus (4.1%). For foreign trips the preferred means of transport was airplane (49.8%), followed by motor vehicles (36.4%) and rail (6.1%). [[Image:F6_Trips made by EU residents by main means of transport, 2024_1.png|thumb|centre|700px|Figure 6: Trips made by EU residents by main means of transport, 2024
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_tttr}}|alt= six pie charts showing trips made by EU residents by main means of transport in 2024, there are three sets of two pie charts each. The first set shows all trips, the second set shows domestic trips and the third set shows foreign trips. In each set one pie chart shows air transport, waterway and land trips and one shows, motor vehicle, bus coach, railway and other land transport. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]]
[[Image:T4_Trips made by EU residents by main means of transport, 2024.png|thumb|centre|800px|Table 4: Trips made by EU residents by main means of transport, 2024
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_tttr}}|alt= A table showing the trips made by EU residents by main means of transport in 2024, in the EU and EU countries. The columns show the share by type of transport, air, waterway and land and the share by type of land transport, railway, bus coach, motor vehicle and other land transport. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] === In 2024 tourism continued recovering from the COVID-19 crisis === The main trends in tourism by EU residents for the period 2007-2024 are shown in Figure 7. Overall, the 2008-09 global economic crisis did not strongly affect EU residents' tourism. Following slight drops each year between 2009 and 2015, in 2016 the number of trips and nights spent started recovering and regained the levels existing prior to the economic crisis. In 2019 compared with 2007, the number of trips and nights spent increased by 6.4% and 1.5% respectively. However, tourism has developed very differently depending on whether the trips were made for personal or professional purposes.
The COVID-19 crisis strongly affected EU residents’ tourism in 2020, with drops of 37% in the number or trips and the number of nights and even higher drops for business trips, compared with the previous year. The slow recovery started in 2021, when the number of trips increased by 22.6% compared with 2020, while the number of nights increased by 19.6% during the same period. The recovery continued in 2022 and 2023. In 2023, the number of tourism trips made by Europeans surpassed the pre-pandemic level of 2019 by 0.5%, while the number of nights, even though they increased compared with the previous years, they were still slightly below pre-pandemic levels (-0.4%). The business trips and nights recorded even slower recovery compared with personal trips and nights.
In 2024, the upward trend in tourism continued, with the number of tourism nights and trips rising by around 4-5% compared to 2019. The increase was particularly notable in personal trips and nights, while the business trips remained below pre-pandemic levels, showing a decrease of 1.3% for trips and 8.0% for nights. However, when comparing with 2023, business trips increased by 11.6% and the business nights by 6.4%, indicating a gradual recovery in the business tourism sector. [[Image:F7_Trends in number of trips, nights spent and average duration of trips made by EU residents, 2007-2024 (index 2007=100).png|thumb|centre|700px|Figure 7: Trends in number of trips, nights spent and average duration of trips made by EU residents, 2007-2024
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_ttq}}, {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_tttot}}, {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_tnq}}, {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_tntot}}|alt= Three line charts showing the Trends in number of trips, nights spent and average duration of trips made by EU residents from 2007 to 2024. The first chart shows all trips, it has three lines, total trips, total nights and average duration; the second chart shows personal trips, it has three lines, personal trips, personal nights and average duration; and the third chart shows business trips, it has three lines business trips, business nights and average duration. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] === Source data for tables and graphs=== *[[Media:Characteristics of trips_2024 data.xlsx|Download Excel file]] [[Image:Microsoft_Excel_2010_Logo.png|20px|link=]] ===Data sources=== '''Collection of annual data on trips of EU residents''' The collection consists of harmonised data collected by the EU countries in the frame of the {{Template:EurLex|code=CELEX:32011R0692:EN:NOT|title=Regulation (EU) No 692/2011}} of the European Parliament and of the Council concerning European statistics on [[Glossary:European_statistics_on_tourism|tourism]]. The scope of observation for data on tourism trips are all tourism trips with at least 1 overnight stay, made by the [[Glossary:Resident|resident population]] aged 15 years and over. It includes trips made for private or professional purpose, outside the usual environment. ===Context=== The EU is a major tourist destination, with 6 EU countries among the world's top 10 destinations for holidaymakers, according to [https://www.e-unwto.org/toc/wtobarometereng/22/3 UN Tourism] data. Tourism is an important activity in the EU which contributes to employment and economic growth, as well as to the development of rural, peripheral or less-developed areas. Tourism is estimated to account for 4.5% to the EU's gross value added. These characteristics drive the demand for reliable and harmonised statistics on this activity, as well as within the wider context of regional policy and sustainable development policy areas. ===Other articles=== *[[Tourism trips of Europeans]] (online publication) *[[Tourism|All articles on tourism statistics]] ===Publications=== *[http://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/tourism/publications Recent Eurostat publications on tourism] ===Selected Datasets=== *Tourism [https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/main/data/database?node_code=t_tour (t_tour)], see: :{{Template:Publication|code=tin00188|title=Trips by purpose (tin00188)}} :{{Template:Publication|code=tin00189|title=Trips by duration of the trip (tin00189)}} :{{Template:Publication|code=tin00191|title=Nights spent by purpose (tin00191)}} :{{Template:Publication|code=tin00192|title=Nights spent by duration of the trip (tin00192)}} ===Database=== *[https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/tourism/database Tourism (tour)], see "Trips of EU residents - annual data": :Tourism trips (tour_dem_tt) : Tourism nights (tour_dem_tn) ===Thematic section=== *[{{Template:Dedicated section|dedicated_section=tourism}} Tourism statistics] ===Methodology=== *{{Template:Esms|code=tour_dem_esms|title= Trips of EU residents - annual data}} (ESMS metadata file — tour_dem_esms) ===Legislation=== *With 2012 as reference year: :*{{Template:EurLex|code=CELEX:32011R0692:EN:NOT|title=Regulation (EU) No 692/2011}} of 6 July 2011 concerning European statistics on tourism and repealing Council Directive 95/57/EC. ([https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/LSU/?uri=CELEX:32011R0692 Summary]) :*{{Template:EurLex|code=CELEX:32011R1051:EN:NOT|title=Regulation (EU) No 1051/2011}} of 20 October 2011 implementing Regulation (EU) No 692/2011 concerning European statistics on tourism, as regards the structure of the quality reports and the transmission of the data. *Previous legal acts (concerning reference periods before 2012): :*{{Template:EurLex|code=CELEX:31995L0057:EN:NOT|title=Directive 95/57/EC}} of 23 November 1995 on the collection of statistical information in the field of tourism :*{{Template:EurLex|code=CELEX:31999D0035:EN:NOT|title=Commission Decision 1999/35/CE}} of 9 December 1998 on the procedures for implementing Council Directive 95/57/EC on the collection of statistical information in the field of tourism. :*{{Template:EurLex|code=CELEX:32004D0883:EN:NOT|title=Commission Decision 2004/883/CE}} of 10 December 2004 adjusting the Annex to Council Directive 95/57/EC on the collection of statistical information in the field of tourism as regards country lists. :*{{Template:EurLex|code=CELEX:32006L0110:EN:NOT|title=Directive 2006/110/EC}} of 20 November 2006 adapting Directives 95/57/EC and 2001/109/EC in the field of statistics, by reason of the accession of Bulgaria and Romania ===External links=== *[http://eur-lex.europa.eu/LexUriServ/LexUriServ.do?uri=CELEX:52007DC0621:EN:NOT Agenda for a sustainable and competitive European tourism] (Communication from the European Commission, October 2007) *[http://ec.europa.eu/growth/sectors/tourism/index_en.htm European Commission - title: Tourism statistics - expenditure
text:
Data extracted in November 2025. Planned article update: November 2026. In 2024, EU residents spent an estimated €618 billion on tourism trips, mostly on trips abroad (58%). EU residents spent 83% of their tourism expenditure on trips inside Europe (76% inside the EU). Europeans spent on average €303 on a domestic trip and €1 053 on a foreign trip in 2024. [[Image:F4_Tourism expenditure and trips of EU residents by destination, 2024 (%).png|thumb|center|500px|Total expenditure by destination, EU, 2024 (%)
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_extotw}}|alt= Pie chart showing tourism expenditure of EU residents by destination, namely, domestic, other EU countries, rest of Europe, Africa, America, Asia and Oceania as percentages for the year 2024. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] This article is part of the [[Glossary:Eurostat|Eurostat]] online publication '''[[Tourism trips of Europeans]]'''. The publication provides recent statistics on tourism [[Glossary:Demand side tourism statistics|demand]] in the [[Glossary:European Union (EU)|European Union (EU)]] and [[Glossary:EFTA|EFTA]] countries. The other articles in this online publication analyse physical flows of [[Glossary:Tourist|tourists]]. This one adds a monetary dimension by taking a closer look at the expenditure of EU [[Glossary:Resident|residents]] during [[Glossary:tourism|tourism]] trips made in 2024. In the context of the article, all expenditure for a given trip refers to individual expenditure (not household expenditure or the expenditure of a travel party). The expenditure is allocated to the [[Glossary:Main country of destination|main country of destination]], no matter in which country the service provider is based or where the turnover or added value was created. For example, if an individual uses an airline carrier, travel agency or tour operator based in a country other than that of the main destination, this expenditure will be allocated to the main country of destination, not to the country of the airline carrier, travel agency or tour operator. === Nearly half of Europeans' tourism expenditure is spent by German and French tourists === In 2024, EU residents spent an estimated €618 [[Glossary:Billion|billion]] on tourism trips (see Table 1), 11% more than in the previous year. Of this, they spent 42% on trips within their own [[Glossary:country of residence|country of residence]] ([[Glossary:Tourism|domestic tourism]]) and 58% on trips abroad ([[Glossary:Tourism|outbound tourism]]). However, domestic trips represented much more of the total number of trips (71%), while trips abroad represented 29% - see the article on the [[Tourism statistics - characteristics of tourism trips|characteristics of tourism trips]]. [[Image:T1_Tourism expenditure of EU residents by destination (domestic_foreign) and by duration of the trip, 2024_1.png|thumb|center|800px|Table 1: Tourism expenditure of EU residents by destination (domestic/foreign) and by duration of the trip, 2024
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_extot}}|alt= A table showing Tourism expenditure of EU residents by destination, both domestic and foreign, and by duration of the trip in 2024 in the EU and EU countries. For more details, please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] In 16 of the EU countries, residents spent half or more of the tourism expenditure during 2024 on trips abroad (see Figure 1). The highest share for foreign expenditure was observed for Luxembourg (99%), followed by Belgium (92%), Malta (91%), Cyprus (87%), Latvia (83%) and the Netherlands (82%). The residents of Romania and Greece spent more than 70% of their total tourism expenditure on domestic trips. [[Image:F1_Tourism expenditure of EU residents by destination (domestic_foreign), 2024 (% in total expenditure).png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 1: Tourism expenditure of EU residents by destination (domestic/foreign), 2024 (% in total expenditure)
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_extot}}|alt= A vertical stacked bar chart showing Tourism expenditure of EU residents by destination, both domestic and foreign, in 2024 in the EU and EU countries. The stacks show domestic trips and foreign trips. For more details, please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] In all countries, most tourism expenditure occurred during longer trips of 4 or more nights (EU average: 73%), with residents of Belgium, Greece, Luxembourg and the Netherlands having spent more than 80 % of their tourism expenditure for long trips. For each tourism trip, Europeans spent on average €518 per person (see Table 2), 7% more than in the previous year. Broken down by destination, they spent €303 on average on a domestic trip and €1 053 on a foreign trip. The average spent per night (and per person) was €104 (€78 on average for each domestic tourism night and €135 a night on average for trips abroad). [[Image:T2_Average tourism expenditure of EU residents per trip and per night, by destination (domestic_foreign), 2024 (€).png|thumb|center|800px|Table 2: Average tourism expenditure of EU residents per trip and per night, by destination (domestic/foreign), 2024 (€)
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_extot}}|alt= A table showing Average tourism expenditure of EU residents per trip and per night, by destination, both domestic and foreign, in 2024 in the EU and EU countries. For more details, please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] Per trip, tourists from Luxembourg spent the most (€1 300), followed by Austrians (€871), Belgians (€787) and German tourists (€729), while under €270 per trip was spent by residents of Lithuania, Czechia and Latvia (see Figure 2). Domestic tourism expenditure per trip was highest in Austria (€467), followed by Sweden (€423). The highest spenders per foreign tourism trip (€1 000 or more) were tourists from Sweden, Luxembourg, Austria, Germany, Cyprus, Finland, Estonia, France and Spain. Residents of Luxembourg, Austria, Sweden, Ireland, Malta, Estonia and Cyprus spent at least €130 per night on average during their tourism trips, while residents of Portugal, Lithuania, Poland, Czechia and Greece spent less than €70 (see Figure 3). German and French tourists were the highest spenders in absolute terms. Their expenditure accounted for nearly half (49%) of the tourism expenditure of all EU residents. This share is more than the proportion of German and French tourists in the total number of trips (43%) or overnight stays (45%) – see the article on the [[Tourism statistics - characteristics of tourism trips|characteristics of tourism trips]]. [[Image:F2_Average tourism expenditure of EU residents per trip, 2024 (€)_1.png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 2: Average tourism expenditure of EU residents per trip, 2024 (€)
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_extot}}|alt= A vertical bar chart showing the Average tourism expenditure of EU residents per trip in 2024 in euro in the EU and EU countries. For more details, please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]]
[[Image:F3_Average tourism expenditure of EU residents per night, 2024 (€).png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 3: Average tourism expenditure of EU residents per night, 2024 (€)
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_extot}}|alt= A vertical bar chart showing Average tourism expenditure of EU residents per night in 2024 in euro in the EU and EU countries. For more details, please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] === Europeans spend 76% of their total tourism expenditure on trips inside the EU === In 2024, intra-EU tourism accounted for 92% of all tourism trips (71% of which were domestic trips and 21% trips to another EU country). In terms of expenditure, however, domestic trips accounted for 42% of total tourism expenditure (see Figure 4), all EU destinations (including domestic) for 76% and destinations outside the EU for 24% (compared with only 8% of the number of tourism trips). [[Image:F4_Tourism expenditure and trips of EU residents by destination, 2024 (%).png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 4: Tourism expenditure and trips of EU residents by destination, 2024 (%)
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_extotw}}, {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_ttw}}|alt= A pie chart showing the Tourism expenditure and trips of EU residents by destination in 2024. The segments show domestic, other EU countries, rest of Europe, Africa, America, Asia and Oceania. For more details, please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] Europeans travelling to foreign continents spent most on trips to Asia and America (each with 6% of total expenditure by EU residents on tourism trips), followed by Africa (4%). European destinations outside the EU accounted for 7% of all of the tourism expenditure of EU residents. === Expenditure on accommodation accounts for one-third of the tourism budget of EU residents === Accommodation took up 35% of tourism expenditure, while transport accounted for 27% and miscellaneous other costs for 38% (see Figure 5). Looking at domestic and foreign trips separately, the share of transport expenditure was higher by 11 percentage points for foreign trips than for domestic trips. The difference in the share of accommodation expenditure was less significant (+1 percentage point for foreign trips). [[Image:F5_Tourism expenditure of EU residents by type of expenditure, 2024 (%).png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 5: Tourism expenditure of EU residents by type of expenditure, 2024 (%)
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_extot}}|alt= A group of three pie charts showing the Tourism expenditure of EU residents by type of expenditure in 2024. One pie chart shows all trips, the second domestic trips and the third, foreign trips. All three have segments showing transport, accommodation and other. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] On average, expenditure per trip was higher for trips for which the main accommodation was rented (see Figure 6). The average cost of trips spent at hotels was €785 and in rented houses or apartments was €651, while trips spent at an own holiday home cost €272 on average and those spent at accommodation provided free of charge by friends or relatives cost €214. [[Image:F6_Average tourism expenditure per trip by type of accommodation, EU, 2024 (€).png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 6: Average tourism expenditure per trip by type of accommodation, EU, 2024 (€)
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_extot}} {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_ttac}}|alt=A horizontal bar chart showing the Average tourism expenditure per trip by type of accommodation in the EU in 2024 in euro. There are 7 bars showing different types of rented and non-rented accommodation. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] For trips where the main means of accommodation was rented accommodation, the average expenditure per night per person on accommodation was €60 – ranging from €26 per night for trips spent mainly at campsites to €77 for trips spent mainly at hotels (see Figure 7). [[Image:F7_Average expenditure per night on accommodation for trips of EU residents, by type of rented accommodation, EU, 2024 (€)_1.png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 7: Average expenditure per night on accommodation for trips of EU residents, by type of rented accommodation, EU, 2024 (€)
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_exac}}|alt= A horizontal bar chart showing the Average expenditure per night on accommodation for trips of EU residents, by type of rented accommodation in the EU in 2024 in euro. There are 4 bars showing different types of rented accommodation. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] === Age makes a slight difference to the average expenditure per trip === Tourists under 45 years old accounted for less tourism expenditure (43% of expenditure made by all age groups) than tourism trips in 2024 (47%). On average tourists of this age group spent €476 per trip, with the youngest (15-24 years old) spending the least (€421) (see Figure 8 and Figure 9). The rest (and older) of the age groups spent €555 on average per trip, with tourists aged from 55 to 64 years spending the most (€574). [[Image:F8_Share_of_the_age_group_in_the_total_number_of_tourism_trips_and_expenditure,_EU,_2024_(%).png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 8: Share of the age group in the total number of tourism trips and expenditure, EU, 2024 (%)
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_exage}} {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_ttage}}|alt= A double horizontal bar chart showing the Share of the age group in the total number of tourism trips and expenditure in the EU in 2024 as a percentage. The bars show 6 different age categories, and each age category has trips and expenditure. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]]
[[Image:F9_Average tourism expenditure per trip by age group and destination, EU, 2024 (€).png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 9: Average tourism expenditure per trip by age group and destination, EU, 2024 (€)
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_exage}}|alt= A triple horizontal bar chart showing the Average tourism expenditure per trip by age group and destination in the EU in 2024 in euro. The bars show 6 different age categories, and each age category has domestic trips, foreign trips and all countries of the world. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] === Business travel accounts for 13% of total tourism expenditure in 2024 === Holiday, leisure and recreation trips accounted for the majority of tourism expenditure (68%) in 2024 (see Figure 10). At €660, they recorded the highest average expenditure per trip, even higher than expenditure on business trips (€631), while the expenditure per night (see Figure 12) was 2.1 times higher for business trips than for trips for personal purposes (€203 per night versus €112 per night). [[Image:F10_Share of trips and expenditure by purpose of the trip, EU, 2024 (%).png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 10: Share of trips and expenditure by purpose of the trip, EU, 2024 (%)
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_expur}} {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_ttpur}}|alt= A double horizontal bar chart showing Share of trips and expenditure by purpose of the trip in the EU in 2024 in euro. The bars show 4 different purpose categories, and each purpose category has trips and expenditure. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]]
[[Image:F11_Average expenditure per trip by purpose of the trip, EU, 2024 (€).png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 11: Average expenditure per trip by purpose of the trip, EU, 2024 (€)
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_expur}}|alt= A horizontal bar chart showing Average expenditure per trip by purpose of the trip in the EU in 2024 in euro. There are 5 bars showing the average expenditure for different purposes of the trip. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] Business trips accounted for 13% of tourism expenditure in 2024 and had a similar share (10%) in the total of trips. Visits to relatives and friends, on the other hand, accounted for only 15% of all tourism expenditure, but they represented 32% of all tourism trips (accommodation is more likely to be offered for free on such trips). A typical visit to relatives and friends costs nearly half compared with the average tourism trip for personal reasons (€252 compared with €505) (see Figure 11). [[Image:F12_Average expenditure per night by purpose of the trip, EU, 2024 (€).png|thumb|center|700px|Figure 12: Average expenditure per night by purpose of the trip, EU, 2024 (€)
''Source:'' Eurostat {{Stable link|title=|code=tour_dem_expur}}|alt= A horizontal bar chart showing average expenditure per night by purpose of the trip in the EU in 2024 in euro. There are 5 bars showing the average expenditure for different purposes of the trip. For more details please use the link to the source dataset code below the image.]] === Source data for tables and graphs=== *[[Media:Tourism expenditure_2024data.xlsx|Download Excel file]] [[Image:Microsoft_Excel_2010_Logo.png|20px|link=]] === Data sources=== '''Collection of annual data on trips of EU residents''' The collection consists of harmonised data collected by the EU countries in the frame of the {{Template:EurLex|code=CELEX:32011R0692:EN:NOT|title=Regulation (EU) No 692/2011}} of the European Parliament and of the Council concerning European statistics on [[Glossary:European_statistics_on_tourism|tourism]]. The scope of observation for data on tourism trips are all tourism trips with at least 1 overnight stay, made by the [[Glossary:Resident|resident population]] aged 15 and over. It includes trips made for private or professional purpose, outside the usual environment. ===Context=== The EU is a major tourist destination, with 6 EU countries among the world's top 10 destinations for holidaymakers, according to [https://www.e-unwto.org/toc/wtobarometereng/22/3 UN Tourism] data. Tourism is an important activity in the EU which contributes to employment and economic growth, as well as to the development of rural, peripheral or less-developed areas. Tourism is estimated to account for 4.5% to the EU's gross value added. These characteristics drive the demand for reliable and harmonised statistics on this activity, as well as within the wider context of regional policy and sustainable development policy areas. ===Other articles=== *[[Tourism trips of Europeans]] (online publication) *[[:Category:Tourism|All articles on tourism statistics]] ===Publications=== *[http://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/tourism/publications Recent Eurostat publications on tourism] ===Selected Datasets=== *Tourism [https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/main/data/database?node_code=t_tour (t_tour)], see: :{{Template:Publication|code=tin00194|title=Expenditure by category of expenditure (tin00194)}} :{{Template:Publication|code=tin00195|title=Average expenditure per trip (tin00195)}} :{{Template:Publication|code=tin00196|title=Average expenditure per night(tin00196)}} ===Database=== *[https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/tourism/database Tourism (tour)], see: :Trips of EU residents - annual data ::Tourism trips (tour_dem_tt) ::Tourism nights (tour_dem_tn) ::Expenditure on tourism trips (tour_dem_ex) ===Dedicated section=== *[{{Template:Dedicated section|dedicated_section=tourism}} Tourism statistics] ===Data visualisations=== *[http://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/cache/RSI/# Select statistical domain 'Tourism' (top right)] ===Methodology=== *{{Template:Esms|code=tour_dem_esms|title=Trips of EU residents - annual data}} (ESMS metadata file — tour_dem_esms) ===Legislation=== *With 2012 as reference year: :*{{Template:EurLex|code=CELEX:32011R0692:EN:NOT|title=Regulation (EU) No 692/2011}} of 6 July 2011 concerning European statistics on tourism and repealing Council Directive 95/57/EC.
